You're only 18, Don't be so hard on yourself. I know it probably feels like you're falling behind, especially when you're trying your hardest and still don't see results you want. But you're not supposed to have everything figured out yet. Keep working on yourself but don't forget to actually live your life along the way. You don't have to become someone worthy of anothers love or happiness. Love yourself. and don't let loneliness convince you that you'll always be alone. Give yourself time to grow, make mistakes, experience things, and figure out who you are. One day, you'll look back and realize that this version of you was just the beginning. 
 
I spent many years dwelling on the fact that I wasn't where I wanted to be. But the truth is, I was exactly where I needed to be to become the person I wanted to be. I had just become so obsessed with everything I lacked that I could no longer appreciate the value of what I had. No obligations. No commitments. Nothing to lose. The freedom to try, do, and learn almost anything. The freedom to build a life on my own terms. Sometimes, we're so focused on getting somewhere that we forget to appreciate where we are. Even when where we are genuinely sucks, there's still something worth appreciating. Something to be grateful for. Because the truth is, you might always be chasing "where you want to be". And that's not necessarily a bad thing. If you're not chasing something, what is there left to strive for? There's always another level, another goal, another version of yourself you want to become. 
 
The person walking wants a bike. The person with a bike wants a car. The person with a car wants a supercar. The supercar owner wants a boat. The boat owner wants a yacht. The yacht owner wants a private jet. And somewhere along the way, the person with the jet might realize they've lost most of the people they used to connect with because they've built a life they no longer know how to share with them. The point isn't to stop wanting more. It's to stop believing that more is what will finally make you happy. 
 
Learn to appreciate the journey between where you are and where you want to be. That space in between is sacred. It's where you learn who you are, discover what matters to you, and develop the character to handle the things you're working toward. Fall in love with your process. Your journey. Romanticize the little things. Celebrate the small wins. Enjoy the freedom you have right now, because some of the things you take for granted today might be the things you miss most when your life looks completely different. And please understand that you don't have to be happy every second of the journey. You're allowed to feel lost, and have days when everything feels pointless. Appreciating your life doesn't mean pretending everything is perfect. It means learning not to let everything that's missing blind you to everything that's still possible. And more importantly, not allowing the fact that everything is imperfect to keep you from finding true inner peace. 
 
You have so much time to figure things out. So much room to fail, experiment, change directions, and start again. You think you're behind. But you're not. Your potential is limitless. You can build an incredible life for yourself, but don't put off being happy. You are living your life right now, not someday when you've finally become the person you want to be. 
 
Stay true to yourself. Keep growing. Keep moving forward. And give yourself permission to enjoy being the person you are along the way. Because the journey isn't just the thing you have to get through to reach your destination. The journey is your life. And it's happening right now.

October 10th, 2026.

So, I got into medschool, not exactly what i wanted but it's just as hard as I pictured it would be. Tried to get in, 3 entire years and now I got it but that didn't give me that "accomplished" feeling...

For anyone that reads this, time's on your side, don't rush a relationship or a career, you're young still, I know you feel the urge to do more and more but that'll only bring unhappiness to your life, and can safely say so myself as I have experienced it.

Life's hard enough so don't be too hard on yourselves, and instead show yourselves some very deserved love. Mistakes happen, mistakes are what makes who we are. We will do very regrettable things, say a lot of stuff we don't mean, but the important thing is, that you try and fix your mistakes and forgive yourselves and those who may do or say against you, no sense in opening old wounds just to prove they still hurt. Be good and show love to others, we really do need other people on our lives aside from ourselves. A grade, a conversation, an opinion, a discussion, bad parenting, bad relationships, bad experiences, nothing of that has to decide who y'all are, it's your good actions and choices that will. Don't be sheep. Come out of autopilot and take the damn bull by the horns, put limits to toxic people in your lives, burn those bridges if needed. You only got this one life.

You may come across my comment in a few days, weeks, months, years even, but that doesn't matter, it is some advice from someone that never thought their life could amount to this much and would've loved for someone to tell them to just take it easy.
